title: The committee stage
question: How many money files does each committee send to the Board, and how often is the committee itself divided?
finding: Committees took 3,462 roll calls to recommend a money file or send it on, covering 3,455 files; the Budget and Finance Committee took 2,417 of them. A member voted no in 16 (0.5%), and in 3 the motion to recommend failed. Of the 16 files with a divided committee vote, 13 went on to a Board vote and 8 of those drew a no there as well. 66 roll calls sent a file on without a recommendation and 1 with a recommendation of “do not pass”; 209 sent it as a committee report.
how: Every committee roll call on a money file whose action is to recommend it, recommend it as amended, or refer it without recommendation (the shared definition of a committee-stage vote). Committee names are as the vote pages print them. A roll call is divided when at least one member is printed as voting No. Votes on amendments and continuances are not counted here; 13 of those had a no. The Rules of Order say: “A committee may send legislation to the full Board with its recommendation, or without recommendation, or with a recommendation of do not pass.”
limits: Committees usually have three members, so one no is a third of the vote; disagreement at this stage can also show up as an amendment or a continuance, which this table does not count. A unanimous recommendation is the ordinary result. 2 roll calls are printed with the result “Fail” although every member listed voted aye and the text says the motion carried: the record looks wrong there, not the vote, and they are counted as passed. 3 committee recommendations on money files are among the roll calls still without names and are missing from this table. For 332 roll calls the Clerk’s vote page says “by the following vote” and lists no member, 306 of them dated 2016-04-13 to 2016-07-26; 315 were read instead from the vote lines in the Clerk’s published minutes of the same meeting, and 17 remain without member votes and are counted nowhere here. 1 money file (160358) whose final passage is among them is left out of the counts, and none is counted as unanimous. 104 of the final votes counted here were read from the minutes. The Rules of Order on disk are the edition effective June 30, 2026; earlier editions are not on disk. Amounts, parties and dates taken from Board file titles are read by machine: in a hand check of 50 titles, 11 had at least one field read wrongly (4 after later fixes).
